contexts.text: These feasts took place in the holy place... and signified the communication, conjunction and appropriation of celestial goods...
He made them a feast () = dwelling together. Feasts, mentioned in the Word, = dwelling together. Illustrated. AC 3456.
A feast of fat things = dwelling with the Lord in good and truth.

The feasts from the sanctified things... represented the dwelling together of the Lord with man in the holy things of love represented by the sacrifices. The like was afterwards represented by the Holy Supper, which, in the Primitive Church, was called a feast.
Feasts take place among a number who are together in love and charity...
Dinner, supper, feast = the good of charity, in which is the dwelling together of the Lord with man.
Abraham made a great feast () = dwelling together and union... It = union also, because it treats of the Lord. AC 2649.
Feasts with the ancients were nothing else.

He made a feast () = initiation. (For) a feast = appropriation and conjunction; here, initiation, because this precedes conjunction... The feasts of ancient times... signified initiation into mutual love... The nuptial feasts signified initiation into marriage love; and the holy feasts, initiation into spiritual and celestial love; and this because to feast, or eat and drink, signified appropriation and conjunction. Illustrated.
Under Evening, see this reference.
See Eat up.

That there might be represented the heavenly feast; that is, conjunction through the good of love and of charity. This is signified by the Holy Supper, which succeeded in place of the sacrifices and of the feasts from the sanctified things.
He made a feast for all his servants () = initiation and conjunction with the exterior Natural. A feast = initiation to conjunction.

Feasts formerly took place for various reasons; and there was signified by them initiation into mutual love, and thus conjunction. They also took place on birthdays; and there was then represented by them birth anew or regeneration, which is the conjunction of the interiors with the exteriors in a man through love, consequently the conjunction of Heaven with the world in him...
Eatings and feasts = conjunction; in special, initiation to conjunction. References.
A feast of fat things; a feast of lees ()... A feast = Heaven and conjunction there with the Angels through love and charity. References.

By to eat is here meant the eating which in the Word is called a feast. Eatings or feasts took place with the ancients within the Church for the sake of conjunction and of confirmation in good. References.
When they made ready calves in their feasts of charity...

In general, feasts, both dinners and suppers, took place in ancient times within the Church, in order that they might be consociated and conjoined as to love, and that they might instruct each other in the things of love and faith... Such, at that time, were the delights attending meals; and they were the end for the sake of which the dinners and suppers were held. Both mind and body were thus unanimously and correspondently nourished. From this they had health and long life; also intelligence and wisdom; and also communication with Heaven; with some, open communication with Angels. But as in course of time all internal things vanish, and pass into external things, so did the ends of feasts and meals, which at this day are not for the sake of any spiritual conjunction, but for the sake of worldly conjunctions; that is, gains, honours, and pleasures. Hence there is nourishment of the body: but none of the mind.

Eatings, feasts, dinners, and suppers were instituted among the ancients, in order that they might be consociated by such things as are of wisdom and intelligence. (References.) Hence feasts, dinners, and suppers, in the Word, = consociations as to faith and love. Illustrated.
In Heaven... there are feasts.

In the Primitive Church... there were dinners and suppers... which were called feasts, being instituted that they might be glad from the heart together, and be conjoined with one another. (See Dinner.)

The feasts in the Ancient Churches were feasts of charity, in like manner as in the Primitive Christian Church; in which they strengthened one another to abide in the worship of the Lord from a sincere heart.
The Lord... likened Heaven to feasts, because they made heavenly joy to consist in feasts.
A feast of fat things = the appropriation and communication of goods; and a feast of lees or of the best wine, = the appropriation of truths. AE 1159:3.
Their feasts () = adulterations of good and truth. (Compare AE 601:11.)
(Feasts, etc. as a recreation.)
